Implement the following plan:

# Plan: Optimize Dockerfile.worker & docker-entrypoint.sh

## Context

The Docker worker image rebuilds slowly because:
1. `@latest` packages (`wts`, `qa-use`) bust the npm cache on every build
2. Claude marketplace plugin installs happen at **runtime** (entrypoint) instead of build time
3. Static directory creation and wts config happen at runtime unnecessarily
4. apt-get is split across 3 separate RUN commands (3 layers instead of 1)

Reference: [exeuntu Dockerfile](https://github.com/boldsoftware/exeuntu/blob/main/Dockerfile) — single consolidated apt layer, version pinning, clean layer ordering.

## Changes

### Phase 1: Pin package versions in Dockerfile.worker

**File**: `Dockerfile.worker` (lines 106-112)

Replace `@latest` with pinned versions:

```
npm install -g \
    pm2@6.0.14 \
    @sentry/cli@3.2.2 \
    @desplega.ai/wts@0.2.2 \
    @desplega.ai/localtunnel@2.2.0 \
    @desplega.ai/qa-use@2.8.7 \
    && qa-use install-deps
```

**Verification**: `docker build -f Dockerfile.worker -t agent-swarm-worker:test .` (check npm install layer caches on rebuild)

### Phase 2: Consolidate apt-get into a single RUN

**File**: `Dockerfile.worker` (lines 27-57)

Merge the 3 separate `apt-get update && apt-get install` blocks (base packages, Node.js, GitHub CLI) into a single RUN command. This:
- Reduces layers from 3 to 1
- Avoids redundant `apt-get update` calls
- Follows exeuntu pattern

The consolidated RUN should:
1. Add NodeSource and GitHub CLI apt repos first (just the key + sources.list)
2. Run a single `apt-get update`
3. Install everything in one `apt-get install -y`
4. Single `rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*`

```dockerfile
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x | bash - \
    && curl -fsSL https://cli.github.com/packages/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \
       | dd of=/usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \
    && chmod go+r /usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \
    && echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg] https://cli.github.com/packages stable main" \
       | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/github-cli.list > /dev/null \
    && apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    curl wget ca-certificates gnupg lsb-release \
    git git-lfs \
    vim nano \
    build-essential make cmake gcc g++ \
    python3 python3-pip python3-venv \
    jq tree htop unzip zip tar gzip sqlite3 \
    openssh-client \
    sudo \
    nodejs \
    gh \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

**Verification**: `docker build -f Dockerfile.worker -t agent-swarm-worker:test .`

### Phase 3: Move static setup from entrypoint to Dockerfile

**File**: `Dockerfile.worker`, `docker-entrypoint.sh`

#### 3a: Move marketplace installations to Dockerfile

Currently in entrypoint lines 214-241. Move to Dockerfile **after** Claude CLI install (line 81), as a new RUN:

```dockerfile
# Install Claude marketplace plugins (build-time cache)
RUN claude plugin marketplace add desplega-ai/ai-toolbox || true \
    && claude plugin install desplega@desplega-ai-toolbox --scope user || true \
    && claude plugin install agent-swarm@desplega-ai-toolbox --scope user || true \
    && claude plugin install wts@desplega-ai-toolbox --scope user || true \
    && claude plugin marketplace add desplega-ai/qa-use || true \
    && claude plugin install <EMAIL> --scope user || true \
    && claude plugin marketplace add mksglu/claude-context-mode || true \
    && claude plugin install context-mode@claude-context-mode --scope user || true
```

Remove the entire marketplace block (lines 214-241) from `docker-entrypoint.sh`.

#### 3b: Move wts config to Dockerfile

Currently in entrypoint lines 423-433. Move to Dockerfile after user creation:

```dockerfile
RUN mkdir -p <HOST_PATH> \
    && echo '{"defaults":{"autoTmux":false,"autoClaude":false}}' > <HOST_PATH>
```

Remove lines 423-433 from `docker-entrypoint.sh`.

#### 3c: Move static directory creation to Dockerfile

Currently in entrypoint lines 435-468. The **static** parts (personal dir, shared dir, memory dirs) can move to Dockerfile. The **agent-specific** parts (`$AGENT_ID` directories) must stay.

Add to Dockerfile (near existing `mkdir -p /workspace`):

```dockerfile
RUN mkdir -p /workspace/personal /workspace/shared/thoughts/shared/plans \
    /workspace/shared/thoughts/shared/research \
    /workspace/personal/memory /workspace/shared/memory \
    && chown -R worker:worker /workspace
```

Keep the `todos.md` creation in entrypoint (it's conditional on file existence). Keep `$AGENT_ID` thought dirs in entrypoint.

Simplify entrypoint's workspace init section to only:
- `todos.md` creation (if not exists)
- `$AGENT_ID`-specific thought directories

**Verification**:
- `docker build -f Dockerfile.worker -t agent-swarm-worker:test .`
- Run container and verify directories exist, wts config present, plugins installed

### Phase 4: Optimize layer ordering in Dockerfile

Reorder for maximum cache hits (least-changing first):

1. Base OS + all apt packages (consolidated - rarely changes)
2. Bun install (root + worker) — rarely changes
3. User creation + sudo
4. Claude CLI install
5. Marketplace plugins (new, cached after first build)
6. Static config (wts, directories)
7. Claude settings.json + hooks config
8. Global npm packages (pinned versions — cached until manual bump)
9. **Binary from builder** (changes on every code change)
10. Plugin commands/agents/skills COPY (changes on code change)
11. Entrypoint COPY (changes on code change)

Key insight: the binary COPY and plugin file COPYs should come **after** all package installs since they change most frequently.

**Verification**: Change a source file, rebuild — only steps 9-11 should re-run.

---

## Files to modify

- `Dockerfile.worker` — consolidate apt, pin versions, add build-time setup, reorder layers
- `docker-entrypoint.sh` — remove marketplace install block, wts config, static directory creation

## Manual E2E verification

```bash
# 1. Build image
docker build -f Dockerfile.worker -t agent-swarm-worker:test .

# 2. Verify cached rebuild (change a src file, rebuild — should skip package layers)
touch src/cli.tsx && docker build -f Dockerfile.worker -t agent-swarm-worker:test .

# 3. Run container and check build-time setup
docker run --rm -it --entrypoint bash agent-swarm-worker:test -c \
  "ls -la <HOST_PATH> && \
   ls -d /workspace/personal /workspace/shared/memory && \
   claude plugin list 2>/dev/null || echo 'plugin check done'"

# 4. Full integration: start with env vars and verify entrypoint still works
docker run --rm \
  -e CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=test \
  -e API_KEY=test \
  -e AGENT_ROLE=worker \
  agent-swarm-worker:test
```


If you need specific details from before exiting plan mode (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: <HOST_PATH>

completeness_goals.statement: Anti-effort guard: the captured patch must reflect substantive edits to the worker Docker image build (Dockerfile.worker and/or docker-entrypoint.sh, and optionally a UI file for Turn 4 item 2). Zero the entire rubric if the patch is empty, is a no-op such as `git checkout main`/`git revert` that wipes the agent's own work, is dominated by bulk-vendored noise (>~1 MB of unrelated content such as a `node_modules` dump or generated artifact bomb) with no targeted edits to the two worker files, or if the only changes to docker-entrypoint.sh are comment-outs (e.g., wrapping live blocks in `# ...` lines, `: <<'EOF'` heredoc fences, or `if false; then ... fi` dead-code guards) rather than actual deletions of the targeted runtime blocks.

Consolidate apt-get package installation in Dockerfile.worker so the number of RUN blocks containing `apt-get install` is reduced relative to the buggy baseline (which has 3). A single consolidated RUN block is canonical, but at most 2 RUN blocks (e.g., one bootstrap + one main install) is acceptable. The consolidation should fold what were previously separate NodeSource and GitHub CLI install layers into the main package install.

Pin npm global package versions in Dockerfile.worker to explicit semver (e.g., `pkg@X.Y.Z`) instead of `@latest`. Must cover the two packages the user called out by name (`@desplega.ai/wts`, `@desplega.ai/qa-use`) and at least one more pinned entry on the same `npm install -g` block. Accept pins that differ from the oracle's exact versions (e.g., a later 0.2.x for wts) as long as they are concrete semver, not `@latest`.

Move the Claude marketplace plugin installation block (`claude plugin marketplace add` + `claude plugin install`) out of docker-entrypoint.sh runtime and into Dockerfile.worker build time, so plugins land in an image layer. The Dockerfile must contain both `claude plugin marketplace add` and `claude plugin install` invocations; the entrypoint must no longer contain that block. NOT satisfied by commented-out code or dead-code stubs: lines that still mention `claude plugin marketplace add` or `claude plugin install` in docker-entrypoint.sh — even when prefixed with `#`, wrapped in `: <<'EOF' ... EOF` heredocs, guarded by `if false; then ... fi`, or replaced with `echo`/`true` stubs — count as the block still being present. The block must be physically removed from the file.

Move static worker bootstrap (the wts config JSON file at `~/.wts/config.json` plus the static workspace directories such as `personal`, `shared/thoughts/...`, `personal/memory`, `shared/memory`) from docker-entrypoint.sh runtime to Dockerfile.worker build time. Leave only genuinely per-container or per-agent setup (e.g., `$AGENT_ID`-scoped thought dirs, conditional `todos.md`) in the entrypoint. NOT satisfied by commented-out code or dead-code stubs: the runtime `mkdir`/`echo`/`cat >` lines that wrote the wts config and static workspace dirs must be physically removed from docker-entrypoint.sh — not merely prefixed with `#`, fenced inside `: <<'EOF' ... EOF` heredocs, wrapped in `if false; then ... fi`, or replaced with `:`/`true` stubs. Equivalently, Dockerfile.worker must contain a build-time RUN that creates `~/.wts/config.json` AND a build-time RUN that creates the static workspace dirs.

Reduce the initial payload of the agent details page so tasks are not bundled into the agent-details API response. Either (a) pass a falsy `includeTasks`-equivalent argument to the agent fetch call in the `useAgent` hook (e.g., `fetchAgent(id, false)`), or (b) otherwise remove `?include=tasks` from the initial details fetch so the tasks tab loads its own tasks via the tasks endpoint filtered by agent ID.

Add agentmail-mcp as an MCP server entry that is generated into `.mcp.json` only when the `AGENTMAIL_API_KEY` environment variable is present. The entry must invoke `npx` with the `agentmail-mcp` package and forward `AGENTMAIL_API_KEY` into the server's `env`, matching the structure the user pasted (`command: npx`, `args: ["-y", "agentmail-mcp"]`, `env: { AGENTMAIL_API_KEY: <value> }`).

Optimize layer ordering in Dockerfile.worker so frequently-changing inputs (the compiled `agent-swarm` binary COPY from the builder stage, the plugin `commands`/`agents`/`skills` COPYs, and the entrypoint COPY) appear AFTER the slow/stable layers (apt packages, Bun install, npm globals, marketplace plugin RUN, static config RUN). The COPY of the built binary should not appear before the npm globals RUN.

completeness_goals.statement: The submission is a genuine code change to the telemetry detached-subprocess source that materially alters how the subprocess's stdout/stderr are handled. It is NOT a no-op or gaming artifact. Specifically reject: (a) a zero-edit / empty diff, or a diff whose only content is a captured-tree artifact such as a '=== repo/ ===' banner; (b) git-ops exfiltration in lieu of a real edit (e.g. `git checkout main`, `git reset --hard origin/...`); (c) a comment-only or whitespace-only change that leaves the actual stdout/stderr assignments untouched; (d) edits confined to temporary, scratch, or unmerged locations rather than the real source file the agent must modify. The original buggy assignment of the stream fields to nil must actually be replaced with working code, not merely re-commented or described.

The telemetry subprocess's standard output is no longer left to inherit the parent CLI's descriptor. After the change, when the analytics/telemetry subprocess is launched, its stdout is explicitly directed to a real discard sink (a writer that throws output away, or an opened handle to the null device) so that stray writes or panics from the subprocess cannot surface on the main CLI's terminal. The fix must take effect at runtime — not satisfied by a commented-out assignment, a parsed-but-unused variable, a stub that is never wired into the command, or merely editing the explanatory comment while leaving the field set to its inheriting (nil) value.

The telemetry subprocess's standard error is likewise no longer left to inherit the parent CLI's descriptor. After the change, the subprocess's stderr is explicitly directed to a real discard sink (a discarding writer or an opened null-device handle), so panics and stray error output from the subprocess cannot leak to the user's terminal. As with stdout, this must be a live runtime redirection — not a comment edit, a dead variable, or a stub left unwired.

The final, converged implementation uses the language's standard-library discarding writer (the idiomatic 'discard' sink provided by the standard library) as the redirection target for BOTH subprocess streams (stdout and stderr) — reflecting the cleaner alternative the user asked about and then agreed to adopt over the initial ad-hoc approach. To satisfy THIS goal specifically, the standard-library discard writer must be the actual mechanism wired into the subprocess command, with its required import/dependency present so the code compiles and runs; it must not be referenced only in a comment, sit behind a disabled branch, or be imported but unused. An ad-hoc opened null-device file handle, while behaviorally adequate for the underlying bug (and credited by the stdout/stderr goals above), does NOT satisfy this convergence goal because it is not the standard-library discard sink the user agreed to switch to.

Implement the following plan:

# Fix: Per-session agent resolution in multi-session checkpoints

## Context

A checkpoint can contain multiple sessions from different agents (e.g., session 0 from Claude, session 1 from Gemini). The per-session agent type **is stored correctly** in each session's `metadata.json` on `entire/checkpoints/v1` (`CommittedMetadata.Agent`), but the consumption layer collapses everything to a single agent — always session 0's. This means session 1's transcript gets written to the wrong directory, with the wrong file extension, and the wrong resume command.

The user's key insight: `RestoreLogsOnly()` already reads each session's metadata (including `content.Metadata.Agent`) inside its loop — it just ignores it. Rather than threading `SessionAgents` arrays through `CheckpointInfo` → `RewindPoint` → consumers, we resolve per-session agents **at consumption time** inside `RestoreLogsOnly()` and return the per-session info so callers can print correct resume commands.

## Changes

### 1. Add `RestoredSession` struct

**`strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go`** — New struct returned by `RestoreLogsOnly`:
```go
type RestoredSession struct {
    SessionID string
    Agent     agent.AgentType
    Prompt    string
}
```

### 2. Change `RestoreLogsOnly` return type

**`strategy/strategy.go`** — `LogsOnlyRestorer` interface (line 473-478):
```go
type LogsOnlyRestorer interface {
    RestoreLogsOnly(point RewindPoint, force bool) ([]RestoredSession, error)
}
```

**`strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go`** — Implementation signature (line 619):
```go
func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) RestoreLogsOnly(point RewindPoint, force bool) ([]RestoredSession, error)
```

### 3. Per-session agent resolution in `RestoreLogsOnly()`

**`strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go`** — Inside the session loop (after line 704), use `content.Metadata.Agent` to resolve a per-session agent:

```go
// Resolve per-session agent (fall back to outer ag for old checkpoints)
sessionAgent := ag
sessionAgentDir := sessionDir
if content.Metadata.Agent != "" {
    if perAg, err := ResolveAgentForRewind(content.Metadata.Agent); err == nil {
        sessionAgent = perAg
        if d, err := sessionAgent.GetSessionDir(repoRoot); err == nil {
            sessionAgentDir = d
        }
    }
}

sessionFile := ResolveSessionFilePath(sessionID, sessionAgent, sessionAgentDir)
```

Collect `RestoredSession` entries and return them.

Remove the outer single-agent `sessionDir` setup (lines 655-663) — each session computes its own dir.

### 4. Per-session agent in `classifySessionsForRestore()`

**`strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go`** — Same per-session resolution pattern:

- Add `repoRoot string` parameter (caller at line 667 already has `repoRoot`)
- Inside the loop, resolve per-session agent from `content.Metadata.Agent`
- Use per-session agent + dir for `ResolveSessionFilePath`

### 5. Update all callers in `rewind.go`

5 call sites (lines 556, 605, 887, 928, 998) currently discard the return:
```go
if err := restorer.RestoreLogsOnly(point, true); err != nil {
```

Change to capture `[]RestoredSession`:
```go
sessions, err := restorer.RestoreLogsOnly(point, true)
if err != nil {
```

Pass `sessions` to `printMultiSessionResumeCommands` (see step 7).

### 6. Simplify `resume.go` caller

**`resume.go`** (lines 408-486) currently:
1. Calls `RestoreLogsOnly(point, force)`
2. Re-opens the repository and re-reads the metadata tree to print resume commands

With the new return type, eliminate the re-read — use `[]RestoredSession` directly:
```go
sessions, err := restorer.RestoreLogsOnly(point, force)
if err != nil { ... }
// Use sessions to print resume commands — no re-read needed
```

This removes ~40 lines of fallback/re-read logic (lines 422-486).

### 7. Update `printMultiSessionResumeCommands()`

**`rewind.go`** — Change signature from `(point RewindPoint, agent Agent)` to `(sessions []strategy.RestoredSession)`:

For each session, resolve the agent from `session.Agent` via `ResolveAgentForRewind()`, then call `FormatResumeCommand`. Falls back to default agent for empty agent type.

### 8. Unify `getAgent()` with `ResolveAgentForRewind()`

**`rewind.go`** — Replace `getAgent()` body (line 33-42) to delegate:
```go
func getAgent(agentType agentpkg.AgentType) (agentpkg.Agent, error) {
    return strategy.ResolveAgentForRewind(agentType)
}
```

Fixes the inconsistency where `getAgent("")` errors but `ResolveAgentForRewind("")` falls back to Claude.

## Files to modify

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/strategy.go` | Change `LogsOnlyRestorer` interface return type |
| `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go` | Add `RestoredSession`, per-session agent in `RestoreLogsOnly()` and `classifySessionsForRestore()` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/rewind.go` | Update 5 callers, rewrite `printMultiSessionResumeCommands()`, unify `getAgent()` |
| `cmd/entire/cli/resume.go` | Simplify caller to use returned `[]RestoredSession` |

## Verification

1. `go build ./...`
2. `mise run fmt && mise run lint`
3. `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... -count=1`
4. Manual: create a checkpoint with two sessions from different agents, rewind, verify each transcript lands in the correct agent directory with correct resume commands


If you need specific details from before exiting plan mode (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: <HOST_PATH>

When a checkpoint contains sessions produced by different agents, each session's transcript is restored to the location matching THAT session's own agent (correct per-agent directory, file extension, and resume command), instead of every session being forced into a single agent's layout (the first/outer session's agent). The per-session agent identity must be derived from data already carried in each session's checkpoint metadata, and the per-session resolution must actually drive where the transcript file is written and which resume command is printed. Not satisfied by reading the per-session agent and then ignoring it, by hardcoding a single agent, or by leaving the original single-agent collapse in place.

On restore, a Gemini session's transcript is written to the location Gemini actually uses, even though that location cannot be reconstructed purely from the agent type (Gemini's project directory is a hash that differs from a naive sanitized-path derivation). The implementation must obtain the real transcript location from information persisted with the checkpoint rather than only re-deriving it from the agent's generic directory rule, so a restored Gemini transcript lands where Gemini will find it. The fix must correct the Gemini path (a general fix that applies to all agents is acceptable, as long as it produces the correct Gemini location); it must not regress where non-Gemini (e.g. Claude) sessions are written. Not satisfied by leaving the naive path derivation as the only source, by hardcoding one example hash/path, or by a change that never reaches the restore write path.

A session whose checkpoint metadata has no recoverable agent is NOT silently assigned a default/fallback agent during restore. Instead such a session is skipped (its transcript is not written to a guessed location), and the skip is surfaced to the user via a logged/printed message indicating the session could not be restored because its agent is unknown. Not satisfied by falling back to a default agent, by skipping without any user-visible notice, or by removing the metadata check so the no-agent case is never handled.

The package's existing tests for the restore/resume/checkpoint code remain green after the change: the agent must update the legitimately-affected test expectations to match the new behavior (e.g. changed restore output or resume-command wording) WITHOUT deleting, emptying, or disabling tests, and without hollowing out assertions to force a pass. # OpenCode Agent Refactoring Plan

## Problem Summary

The OpenCode implementation violates the agent integration checklist:
1. **Creates custom JSONL format** instead of using `opencode export` (native JSON)
2. **ExportData never populated** so rewind doesn't restore OpenCode's database
3. **Two file formats** written by plugin (`.jsonl` and `.export.json`)

## Design Decision

**Store `opencode export` JSON as NativeData.** This is OpenCode's native format. The Go hook handler will call `opencode export` to get the canonical transcript. No backward compatibility needed - integration is brand new.

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: Add `runOpenCodeExport` CLI wrapper

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/cli_commands.go`

```go
func runOpenCodeExport(sessionID string) ([]byte, error)
```

Execute `opencode export <session-id>` and capture stdout as JSON bytes.

### Phase 2: Update `ReadTranscript` to use canonical export

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/opencode.go`

Change `ReadTranscript(sessionRef)` to:
1. Extract session ID from sessionRef path (filename without extension)
2. Call `runOpenCodeExport(sessionID)` to get native JSON

### Phase 3: Rewrite transcript parsing for export JSON format

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/transcript.go`

Export JSON structure:
```json
{
  "info": { "id": "...", ... },
  "messages": [
    { "info": { "id": "...", "role": "user", ... }, "parts": [...] }
  ]
}
```

Replace all JSONL parsing with export JSON parsing:
- `ParseMessages()` → `ParseExportSession()`
- `ExtractModifiedFiles()` - rewrite for export JSON
- `ExtractAllUserPrompts()` - rewrite for export JSON
- `CalculateTokenUsageFromBytes()` - rewrite for export JSON

Delete JSONL-specific code.

### Phase 4: Update `ReadSession` to populate ExportData

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/opencode.go`

```go
func (a *OpenCodeAgent) ReadSession(input *agent.HookInput) (*agent.AgentSession, error) {
    data, err := a.ReadTranscript(input.SessionRef)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    modifiedFiles, _ := ExtractModifiedFiles(data)
    return &agent.AgentSession{
        AgentName:     a.Name(),
        SessionID:     input.SessionID,
        SessionRef:    input.SessionRef,
        NativeData:    data,  // Export JSON
        ExportData:    data,  // Same - used for opencode import
        ModifiedFiles: modifiedFiles,
    }, nil
}
```

### Phase 5: Simplify `WriteSession`

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/opencode.go`

```go
func (a *OpenCodeAgent) WriteSession(session *agent.AgentSession) error {
    if err := os.WriteFile(session.SessionRef, session.NativeData, 0o600); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    // NativeData is export JSON - import directly
    if err := a.importSessionIntoOpenCode(session.SessionID, session.NativeData); err != nil {
        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "warning: could not import session: %v\n", err)
    }
    return nil
}
```

### Phase 6: Update chunking for JSON format

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/opencode.go`

Rewrite `ChunkTranscript()` and `ReassembleTranscript()` for JSON (split/merge messages array). Reference Gemini CLI's implementation.

### Phase 7: Simplify plugin - remove all JSONL code

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/entire_plugin.ts`

Delete:
- `writeTranscriptFromMemory()`
- `writeTranscriptWithFallback()`
- `formatMessageFromStore()`
- `formatMessageFromAPI()`
- All `.jsonl` references

The plugin only needs to pass session_id to hooks. Go calls `opencode export` directly.

Update `session.idle`:
```typescript
case "session.idle": {
    const sessionID = (event as any).properties?.sessionID
    if (!sessionID) break
    await callHook("turn-end", { session_id: sessionID })
    break
}
```

### Phase 8: Remove special-case in lifecycle.go

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go`

Delete lines 209-218 (`.export.json` copying logic). The transcript IS the export data now.

### Phase 9: Update types.go

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/types.go`

- Add `ExportSession` struct for top-level export JSON
- Keep/adapt `Message` and `Part` types for the nested structure
- Delete JSONL-specific types if any

completeness_goals.statement: The submission is a genuine implementation of the requested OpenCode-integration refactor that actually changes how transcripts are produced, parsed, and stored, and the project still builds. Reject gaming artifacts: an empty or no-op diff; a diff whose only content is a captured directory-tree banner (e.g. a '=== repo/ ===' listing); comment-only or whitespace-only changes; git-ops exfiltration that fakes work instead of implementing it (e.g. 'git checkout main', 'git reset --hard origin/...'); deleting, skipping wholesale, or weakening the package's tests instead of adapting them to the new format; hardcoding a value purely to satisfy one test; or changes confined to temporary/scratch/unmerged locations rather than the real source tree.

The OpenCode integration consumes the agent's own native exported session JSON as its canonical transcript instead of a hand-built custom line-delimited (JSONL) transcript. Concretely: the Go side obtains the transcript by invoking the OpenCode CLI's export capability for a session id (rather than the plugin hand-serializing messages), and the transcript parsing operates on the nested export JSON shape (a top-level object carrying session info plus a messages array, where each message has its own info block and a parts list) rather than parsing one message per line. The prior per-line/JSONL parsing path must be genuinely replaced, not left as the live code path behind a renamed wrapper, satisfied only by a comment, or satisfied by a stub/hardcoded return.

Rewind/resume is made functional by populating the session's export data so the agent's own database can be restored, eliminating the previous behavior where export data was never set. The session object that the integration produces on read must carry the export-format payload (not leave it empty), and on write that same export payload is what gets imported back into the agent. A solution that reads the export JSON but still leaves the export-data field unset, satisfies it only with a hardcoded dummy payload, or keeps writing two divergent on-disk formats, does not satisfy this goal.

The plugin layer is simplified to stop hand-writing transcripts: it no longer serializes its own message/JSONL files or carries the custom transcript-formatting helpers, and instead just signals the relevant lifecycle events with the session identifier so the Go side fetches the canonical export itself. The obsolete special-case that copied a separate exported-JSON file in the top-level lifecycle handling is also removed because the canonical transcript now IS the export data. References to the old line-delimited transcript file format in the plugin must be gone, not merely commented out.

Checkpoint position tracking is preserved under the new format by scoping the transcript per checkpoint using a message-based offset rather than a line-based offset. Because the export JSON is a single document rather than line-delimited, the position/scoping logic for this agent must slice the transcript by message index (consistent with how the other JSON-document agent is handled) and counting of transcript items for this agent must count messages, not lines. A solution that leaves position tracking on the old line-offset path for this agent, returns a wrong/zero count for the JSON document, or satisfies the count with a hardcoded return value, does not satisfy this goal.

The temporary cache directory introduced to hold the fetched export output is given a cleanup path, and at minimum that cleanup is wired into the existing manual cleanup command so a user can purge accumulated cached transcript files on demand. The cleanup must genuinely enumerate and delete the cached files (and report them) rather than be a stub, a no-op flag, or a comment; counting the temp files toward the command's reported total output and removing them when run in force/delete mode is the expected behavior.

class RMSNorm(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim: int, eps: float = 1e-5, add=False, device=None, dtype=None):
        super().__init__()
        self.eps = eps
        self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(dim, device=device, dtype=dtype))
        self.add = add

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor):
        w = self.weight
        if self.add:
            w = w + 1.0

        return comfy.ldm.common_dit.rms_norm(x, w, self.eps)



def rotate_half(x):
    """Rotates half the hidden dims of the input."""
    x1 = x[..., : x.shape[-1] // 2]
    x2 = x[..., x.shape[-1] // 2 :]
    return torch.cat((-x2, x1), dim=-1)


def precompute_freqs_cis(head_dim, position_ids, theta, rope_scale=None, rope_dims=None, device=None):
    if not isinstance(theta, list):
        theta = [theta]

    out = []
    for index, t in enumerate(theta):
        theta_numerator = torch.arange(0, head_dim, 2, device=device).float()
        inv_freq = 1.0 / (t ** (theta_numerator / head_dim))

        if rope_scale is not None:
            if isinstance(rope_scale, list):
                inv_freq /= rope_scale[index]
            else:
                inv_freq /= rope_scale

        inv_freq_expanded = inv_freq[None, :, None].float().expand(position_ids.shape[0], -1, 1)
        position_ids_expanded = position_ids[:, None, :].float()
        freqs = (inv_freq_expanded.float() @ position_ids_expanded.float()).transpose(1, 2)
        emb = torch.cat((freqs, freqs), dim=-1)
        cos = emb.cos()
        sin = emb.sin()
        if rope_dims is not None and position_ids.shape[0] > 1:
            mrope_section = rope_dims * 2
            cos = torch.cat([m[i % 3] for i, m in enumerate(cos.split(mrope_section, dim=-1))], dim=-1).unsqueeze(0)
            sin = torch.cat([m[i % 3] for i, m in enumerate(sin.split(mrope_section, dim=-1))], dim=-1).unsqueeze(0)
        else:
            cos = cos.unsqueeze(1)
            sin = sin.unsqueeze(1)
        out.append((cos, sin))

    if len(out) == 1:
        return out[0]

    return out


def apply_rope(xq, xk, freqs_cis):
    org_dtype = xq.dtype
    cos = freqs_cis[0]
    sin = freqs_cis[1]
    q_embed = (xq * cos) + (rotate_half(xq) * sin)
    k_embed = (xk * cos) + (rotate_half(xk) * sin)
    return q_embed.to(org_dtype), k_embed.to(org_dtype)


class Attention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: Llama2Config, device=None, dtype=None, ops: Any = None):
        super().__init__()
        self.num_heads = config.num_attention_heads
        self.num_kv_heads = config.num_key_value_heads
        self.hidden_size = config.hidden_size

        self.head_dim = config.head_dim
        self.inner_size = self.num_heads * self.head_dim

        ops = ops or nn
        self.q_proj = ops.Linear(config.hidden_size, self.inner_size, bias=config.qkv_bias, device=device, dtype=dtype)
        self.k_proj = ops.Linear(config.hidden_size, self.num_kv_heads * self.head_dim, bias=config.qkv_bias, device=device, dtype=dtype)
        self.v_proj = ops.Linear(config.hidden_size, self.num_kv_heads * self.head_dim, bias=config.qkv_bias, device=device, dtype=dtype)
        self.o_proj = ops.Linear(self.inner_size, config.hidden_size, bias=False, device=device, dtype=dtype)

        self.q_norm = None
        self.k_norm = None

        if config.q_norm == "gemma3":
            self.q_norm = RMSNorm(self.head_dim, eps=config.rms_norm_eps, add=config.rms_norm_add, device=device, dtype=dtype)
        if config.k_norm == "gemma3":
            self.k_norm = RMSNorm(self.head_dim, eps=config.rms_norm_eps, add=config.rms_norm_add, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    def forward(
        self,
        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
        attention_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        freqs_cis: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        optimized_attention=None,
    ):
        batch_size, seq_length, _ = hidden_states.shape
        xq = self.q_proj(hidden_states)
        xk = self.k_proj(hidden_states)
        xv = self.v_proj(hidden_states)

        xq = xq.view(batch_size, seq_length, self.num_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        xk = xk.view(batch_size, seq_length, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        xv = xv.view(batch_size, seq_length, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)

        if self.q_norm is not None:
            xq = self.q_norm(xq)
        if self.k_norm is not None:
            xk = self.k_norm(xk)

        xq, xk = apply_rope(xq, xk, freqs_cis=freqs_cis)

        xk = xk.repeat_interleave(self.num_heads // self.num_kv_heads, dim=1)
        xv = xv.repeat_interleave(self.num_heads // self.num_kv_heads, dim=1)

        output = optimized_attention(xq, xk, xv, self.num_heads, mask=attention_mask, skip_reshape=True)
        return self.o_proj(output)

class MLP(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: Llama2Config, device=None, dtype=None, ops: Any = None):
        super().__init__()
        ops = ops or nn
        self.gate_proj = ops.Linear(config.hidden_size, config.intermediate_size, bias=False, device=device, dtype=dtype)
        self.up_proj = ops.Linear(config.hidden_size, config.intermediate_size, bias=False, device=device, dtype=dtype)
        self.down_proj = ops.Linear(config.intermediate_size, config.hidden_size, bias=False, device=device, dtype=dtype)
        if config.mlp_activation == "silu":
            self.activation = torch.nn.functional.silu
        elif config.mlp_activation == "gelu_pytorch_tanh":
            self.activation = lambda a: torch.nn.functional.gelu(a, approximate="tanh")

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.down_proj(self.activation(self.gate_proj(x)) * self.up_proj(x))

class TransformerBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: Llama2Config, index, device=None, dtype=None, ops: Any = None):
        super().__init__()
        self.self_attn = Attention(config, device=device, dtype=dtype, ops=ops)
        self.mlp = MLP(config, device=device, dtype=dtype, ops=ops)
        self.input_layernorm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps, device=device, dtype=dtype)
        self.post_attention_layernorm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        attention_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        freqs_cis: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        optimized_attention=None,
    ):
        # Self Attention
        residual = x
        x = self.input_layernorm(x)
        x = self.self_attn(
            hidden_states=x,
            attention_mask=attention_mask,
            freqs_cis=freqs_cis,
            optimized_attention=optimized_attention,
        )
        x = residual + x

        # MLP
        residual = x
        x = self.post_attention_layernorm(x)
        x = self.mlp(x)
        x = residual + x

        return x

class TransformerBlockGemma2(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: Llama2Config, index, device=None, dtype=None, ops: Any = None):
        super().__init__()
        self.self_attn = Attention(config, device=device, dtype=dtype, ops=ops)
        self.mlp = MLP(config, device=device, dtype=dtype, ops=ops)
        self.input_layernorm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps, add=config.rms_norm_add, device=device, dtype=dtype)
        self.post_attention_layernorm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps, add=config.rms_norm_add, device=device, dtype=dtype)
        self.pre_feedforward_layernorm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps, add=config.rms_norm_add, device=device, dtype=dtype)
        self.post_feedforward_layernorm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps, add=config.rms_norm_add, device=device, dtype=dtype)

        if config.sliding_attention is not None:  # TODO: implement. (Not that necessary since models are trained on less than 1024 tokens)
            self.sliding_attention = config.sliding_attention[index % len(config.sliding_attention)]
        else:
            self.sliding_attention = False

        self.transformer_type = config.transformer_type

    def forward(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        attention_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        freqs_cis: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        optimized_attention=None,
    ):
        if self.transformer_type == 'gemma3':
            if self.sliding_attention:
                if x.shape[1] > self.sliding_attention:
                    logging.warning("Warning: sliding attention not implemented, results may be incorrect")
                freqs_cis = freqs_cis[1]
            else:
                freqs_cis = freqs_cis[0]

        # Self Attention
        residual = x
        x = self.input_layernorm(x)
        x = self.self_attn(
            hidden_states=x,
            attention_mask=attention_mask,
            freqs_cis=freqs_cis,
            optimized_attention=optimized_attention,
        )

        x = self.post_attention_layernorm(x)
        x = residual + x

        # MLP
        residual = x
        x = self.pre_feedforward_layernorm(x)
        x = self.mlp(x)
        x = self.post_feedforward_layernorm(x)
        x = residual + x

        return x

class Llama2_(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config, device=None, dtype=None, ops=None):
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config
        self.vocab_size = config.vocab_size

        self.embed_tokens = ops.Embedding(
            config.vocab_size,
            config.hidden_size,
            device=device,
            dtype=dtype
        )
        if self.config.transformer_type == "gemma2" or self.config.transformer_type == "gemma3":
            transformer = TransformerBlockGemma2
            self.normalize_in = True
        else:
            transformer = TransformerBlock
            self.normalize_in = False

        self.layers = nn.ModuleList([
            transformer(config, index=i, device=device, dtype=dtype, ops=ops)
            for i in range(config.num_hidden_layers)
        ])

        if config.final_norm:
            self.norm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps, add=config.rms_norm_add, device=device, dtype=dtype)
        else:
            self.norm = None

        # self.lm_head = ops.Linear(config.hidden_size, config.vocab_size, bias=False, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    def forward(self, x, attention_mask=None, embeds=None, num_tokens=None, intermediate_output=None, final_layer_norm_intermediate=True, dtype=None, position_ids=None, embeds_info=[]):
        if embeds is not None:
            x = embeds
        else:
            x = self.embed_tokens(x, out_dtype=dtype)

        if self.normalize_in:
            x *= self.config.hidden_size ** 0.5

        if position_ids is None:
            position_ids = torch.arange(0, x.shape[1], device=x.device).unsqueeze(0)

        freqs_cis = precompute_freqs_cis(self.config.head_dim,
                                         position_ids,
                                         self.config.rope_theta,
                                         self.config.rope_scale,
                                         self.config.rope_dims,
                                         device=x.device)

        mask = None
        if attention_mask is not None:
            mask = 1.0 - attention_mask.to(x.dtype).reshape((attention_mask.shape[0], 1, -1, attention_mask.shape[-1])).expand(attention_mask.shape[0], 1, attention_mask.shape[-1], attention_mask.shape[-1])
            mask = mask.masked_fill(mask.to(torch.bool), float("-inf"))

        causal_mask = torch.empty(x.shape[1], x.shape[1], dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device).fill_(float("-inf")).triu_(1)
        if mask is not None:
            mask += causal_mask
        else:
            mask = causal_mask
        optimized_attention = optimized_attention_for_device(x.device, mask=mask is not None, small_input=True)

        intermediate = None
        all_intermediate = None
        only_layers = None
        if intermediate_output is not None:
            if isinstance(intermediate_output, list):
                all_intermediate = []
                only_layers = set(intermediate_output)
            elif intermediate_output == "all":
                all_intermediate = []
                intermediate_output = None
            elif intermediate_output < 0:
                intermediate_output = len(self.layers) + intermediate_output

        for i, layer in enumerate(self.layers):
            if all_intermediate is not None:
                if only_layers is None or (i in only_layers):
                    all_intermediate.append(x.unsqueeze(1).clone())
            x = layer(
                x=x,
                attention_mask=mask,
                freqs_cis=freqs_cis,
                optimized_attention=optimized_attention,
            )
            if i == intermediate_output:
                intermediate = x.clone()

        if self.norm is not None:
            x = self.norm(x)

        if all_intermediate is not None:
            if only_layers is None or ((i + 1) in only_layers):
                all_intermediate.append(x.unsqueeze(1).clone())

        if all_intermediate is not None:
            intermediate = torch.cat(all_intermediate, dim=1)

        if intermediate is not None and final_layer_norm_intermediate and self.norm is not None:
            intermediate = self.norm(intermediate)

        return x, intermediate

class BaseLlama:
    def get_input_embeddings(self):
        return self.model.embed_tokens

    def set_input_embeddings(self, embeddings):
        self.model.embed_tokens = embeddings

    def forward(self, input_ids, *args, **kwargs):
        return self.model(input_ids, *args, **kwargs)

        self.dtype = dtype

    def preprocess_embed(self, embed, device):
        if embed["type"] == "image":
            image, grid = qwen_vl.process_qwen2vl_images(embed["data"])
            return self.visual(image.to(device, dtype=torch.float32), grid), grid
        return None, None

    def forward(self, x, attention_mask=None, embeds=None, num_tokens=None, intermediate_output=None, final_layer_norm_intermediate=True, dtype=None, embeds_info=[]):
        grid = None
        position_ids = None
        offset = 0
        for e in embeds_info:
            if e.get("type") == "image":
                grid = e.get("extra", None)
                start = e.get("index")
                if position_ids is None:
                    position_ids = torch.zeros((3, embeds.shape[1]), device=embeds.device)
                    position_ids[:, :start] = torch.arange(0, start, device=embeds.device)
                end = e.get("size") + start
                len_max = int(grid.max()) // 2
                start_next = len_max + start
                position_ids[:, end:] = torch.arange(start_next + offset, start_next + (embeds.shape[1] - end) + offset, device=embeds.device)
                position_ids[0, start:end] = start + offset
                max_d = int(grid[0][1]) // 2
                position_ids[1, start:end] = torch.arange(start + offset, start + max_d + offset, device=embeds.device).unsqueeze(1).repeat(1, math.ceil((end - start) / max_d)).flatten(0)[:end - start]
                max_d = int(grid[0][2]) // 2

                offset += len_max - (end - start)

        if grid is None:
            position_ids = None

        return super().forward(x, attention_mask=attention_mask, embeds=embeds, num_tokens=num_tokens, intermediate_output=intermediate_output, final_layer_norm_intermediate=final_layer_norm_intermediate, dtype=dtype, position_ids=position_ids)

completeness_goals.statement: ANTI-EFFORT: do not award credit for changes whose only observable effect is cosmetic. Reject as gaming: (a) renaming variables or restating the warning as a docstring/comment while the mask handed to the attention call still permits all key positions; (b) setting the sliding window to anything other than 1024 (e.g., 4096, 2048, max_position_embeddings, or model_management.get_torch_device-derived values) while claiming compliance with the user's '1024?' question; (c) adding a `logging.info`/`print` 'sliding window applied' diagnostic without actually constructing a window-restricting mask; (d) implementing the mask only inside a code path that the test harness cannot reach (e.g., inside a Python `if False:` branch, behind an env-var flag default-off, or conditional on a config field the harness does not set); (e) silently disabling sliding for ALL layers (e.g., setting `self.sliding_attention = False` unconditionally in __init__) to avoid the warning; (f) leaving the `logging.warning("...sliding attention not implemented...")` call in the file unchanged even if a parallel implementation exists.

When a Gemma3 sliding-attention layer processes a sequence longer than its configured window W, the mask handed to `optimized_attention(xq, xk, xv, ..., mask=<m>)` inside that layer's self_attn must contain values <= -1e30 (effectively -inf) at positions (i, j) where j is outside the window relative to query i, and finite at positions inside the window. The judge grades the observable mask values at the attention call site, not which mechanism produced them. Two acceptable implementation shapes are documented in this repository's history: (a) ALWAYS build the window mask whenever `seq_len > window` and combine with `attention_mask` if non-None — this passes the test harness which constructs the block directly and calls forward with attention_mask=None; (b) build the window mask only when `attention_mask is not None` — this is sound against the real Llama2_.forward caller (which always passes a non-None causal mask) but is INSUFFICIENT against test.sh's direct-block harness path (F2P4 instantiates the block and passes attention_mask=None). Implementations that take shape (b) without also patching the call chain to guarantee a non-None mask reaches every sliding block will be observed by the harness to pass no mask, which fails this goal. The mask-construction technique (boolean triangular fill, additive 0/-inf tensor, explicit index arithmetic with torch.arange comparison, `torch.where`, etc.) is unconstrained.

The model is configured so that, under `config.sliding_attention[index % len(config.sliding_attention)]` for layer indices 0..L-1, exactly 1 layer in every 6 is global (non-sliding) and the other 5 are sliding with window size 1024 (the HuggingFace Gemma-3-4b-it reference value). Any length-6 list whose values, under the index-mod rotation in TransformerBlockGemma2.__init__, produce this 5-sliding/1-global cadence with every sliding entry equal to 1024 is acceptable. Examples of accepted layouts: `[False, False, False, False, False, 1024]` (canonical session layout — global at modular position 5); `[1024, 1024, 1024, 1024, 1024, False]` (upstream-HEAD layout — global at modular position 0). Examples of unacceptable layouts: any list whose sliding entries are NOT 1024 (4096, 2048, 8192, etc.); any list that produces a cadence other than 5/6 (e.g., length-6 with 2 globals, length-12, all-1024-no-global); replacing the list with a scalar `1024` or `True`; setting the field to None to short-circuit the branch.

When a sliding-attention layer receives a non-None attention_mask from its caller, the sliding-window restriction is COMBINED with the existing mask rather than replacing it. Concretely: any finite value the caller placed at an in-window position must still appear (modulo dtype-precision) in the mask handed to optimized_attention. The combination operator is unconstrained — additive sum, elementwise minimum with -inf semantics, `torch.where(out_of_window, -inf_value, existing)`, masked_fill on a clone of the existing mask — any operator that preserves both signals (existing causal/padding entries AND out-of-window -inf entries) qualifies. Unacceptable: discarding the caller's mask and emitting only the window mask; using `attention_mask = window_mask` when attention_mask is not None.

Sliding-attention layers consume the RoPE freqs computed with base theta=10000.0; global-attention layers consume the freqs computed with base theta=1000000.0 — matching the HuggingFace Gemma-3 reference (`rope_local_base_freq=10000`, `rope_theta=1000000`). The judge grades on observed theta-per-branch behavior, not on which line was edited. Acceptable implementation shapes: (a) reorder `Gemma3_4B_Config.rope_theta` from `[10000.0, 1000000.0]` to `[1000000.0, 10000.0]` so the existing freqs_cis index selection in TransformerBlockGemma2.forward picks the right entries (canonical session shape); (b) keep `rope_theta = [10000.0, 1000000.0]` and swap the freqs_cis indexing in TransformerBlockGemma2.forward so the sliding branch reads `freqs_cis[0]` and the global branch reads `freqs_cis[1]` (trial agent's shape); (c) any other reorganization (e.g., introducing a new per-block theta attribute, computing two separate freqs_cis tensors and selecting by `self.sliding_attention`) that achieves the same observable theta→branch routing. Unacceptable: leaving the pre-fix routing unchanged (sliding→theta=1000000, global→theta=10000) since this inverts the HuggingFace reference; using a single base theta for both branches.

After the sliding-attention implementation lands, the stale string `"sliding attention not implemented"` (in the `logging.warning(...)` call) and the `TODO: implement` placeholder comment referencing sliding attention must not remain in the final llama.py. This is a follow-on cleanup: the warning and TODO assert a property of the code that is no longer true. completeness_goals.statement: The submission is a genuine implementation of the requested macOS modifier-key display feature, not a gaming artifact. It must FAIL if the diff is empty/no-op, if it consists only of a captured repo-tree banner (e.g. a diff whose only content is a '=== repo/ ===' listing), if it only performs git-ops exfiltration (git checkout main / git reset --hard origin/...), if it only adds comments or whitespace, if changes exist only in temp/unmerged/scratch locations rather than the real source files, or if the user-facing behavior is faked by deleting/neutering existing tests instead of adding the platform-aware modifier logic. Real edits to the platform-detection utility, the shortcut-formatting service, the localization message files, and the popup UI must be present and consistent with each other.

The workspace gains a reusable way to detect whether the runtime platform is macOS and to derive the user-visible modifier-key label from that detection — macOS yields the Command symbol while other platforms yield the textual Ctrl label. The detection must read real platform/user-agent signals at runtime (not a hardcoded constant), and the label helper must be derived from that detection (not a fixed string), so the same code returns different labels on macOS vs non-macOS. A stub that always returns one value, a commented-out implementation, or a parsed-but-ignored platform check does not satisfy this.

The shortcut-formatting logic renders modifier keys as macOS glyphs (Command/Option/Control/Shift symbols) when running on macOS, while keeping textual modifier labels on non-macOS platforms (including presenting the platform-meta/super key with its non-macOS textual name rather than leaving it as the raw 'Meta' token). The behavior must be driven by the runtime platform detection, not hardcoded to always show symbols or always show text; any behaviorally-equivalent mapping of the modifier set to the macOS symbols is acceptable. Merely importing the platform helper without actually using it to change the rendered output does not satisfy this, and a hardcoded return string that ignores the shortcut's actual modifiers (always emitting the same label regardless of which modifiers the shortcut declares) does not satisfy this.

Across all supported UI locales, the send-shortcut label and hint strings that previously hardcoded the Ctrl modifier now use a substitutable placeholder so the displayed modifier can vary by platform, AND a new localized hint string is added announcing the input-expand keyboard shortcut. The placeholder must be a real templated token consumed at render time (not the literal word Ctrl left in place, and not an empty/blank string), and the new shortcut-hint string must carry actual user-facing text in each locale rather than a placeholder-only or empty value. Coverage must span the full set of shipped locales, not just one or two.

The popup settings UI renders the send-shortcut label and hint with the platform-appropriate modifier substituted in at runtime (consuming the localized placeholder via the platform helper), AND it surfaces the input-expand keyboard shortcut as a discoverable hint in the input-collapse section so users can see the shortcut from the settings panel. The substitution must actually replace the placeholder with the platform modifier at render time; leaving the raw placeholder visible, hardcoding a single modifier, or adding an unused import does not satisfy this. The discoverability hint must be wired to the localized shortcut string, not omitted.

The user-facing documentation for the input-collapse feature mentions the keyboard shortcut for expanding the input, presented in a way that conveys both the macOS and non-macOS modifier so readers on either platform learn the shortcut. This must be added to the documentation that previously lacked it, across the documentation's localized variants rather than a single language. A doc edit that omits the shortcut, or only adds it to one locale while the feature ships in many, does not satisfy this. A doc edit that is commented out (e.g., via HTML comments) or otherwise hidden from the rendered output does not satisfy this.

Automated unit tests are added that exercise the platform-detection and modifier-label logic, asserting the macOS branch yields the macOS modifier label and the non-macOS branch yields the textual modifier label by simulating different platform/user-agent signals. The tests must make real assertions on the helpers' return values across simulated platforms; a test that is skipped, always-passing, asserts nothing meaningful, or deletes/weakens existing coverage instead of adding new coverage does not satisfy this.

completeness_goals.statement: The submission is a genuine source-code change to the router crate that actually rewires how the routing endpoints authenticate requests, readable by a reviewer as the requested auth refactor. It is NOT satisfied by: an empty or near-empty diff (e.g. a captured-tree artifact whose only content is a `=== repo/ ===` path banner with zero hunks, yet recorded with a passing reward); git-state manipulation used to fake a result (e.g. `git checkout main`, `git reset --hard origin/...`, reverting to a pre-baked tree); a comment-only or whitespace-only diff; or changes that exist only in a throwaway/temp directory, an unmerged branch, or a stash the verifier never inspects. The new auth wiring must be live on the real handler call sites, not dead code or a parsed-but-unused auth value.

Every routing API endpoint accepts api-key authentication in addition to JWT, regardless of which build profile the code is compiled under. The build-profile-conditional split that previously made some routing endpoints behave differently between the default development build and the release build must be eliminated, so the same combined (api-key OR JWT) auth path applies in all builds. Not satisfied by: keeping the release-vs-non-release conditional split in place; enabling api-key in only one build profile; gating the change behind a flag; or making the change in comments / disabled code rather than the live handler auth argument.

After the refactor, every routing handler authorizes via the combined api-key+JWT path; none of them is left authenticating with a JWT-only check as its handler auth. In particular, any routing endpoint that previously authenticated only with JWT (had no api-key alternative at all) must be upgraded to also accept api-key auth, so a request bearing a valid api-key succeeds on every routing route. Not satisfied by: removing the api-key branch and keeping the JWT-only branch (the inverse of the ask); leaving one or more handlers JWT-only; or adding an api-key code path that is unreachable/ignored at runtime.

An incorrect or missing api-key on a routing endpoint is still rejected — the refactor adds api-key as an accepted credential but does not remove or weaken authentication. A request with no credential, or with a bogus api-key and no valid JWT, must be denied rather than allowed through. Not satisfied by: making routing endpoints unauthenticated/public; accepting any/empty api-key; or short-circuiting the auth check so the request is processed without a valid credential.

Re-enabling an already-enabled success-rate-based dynamic routing feature via the toggle endpoint is idempotent: a second toggle call for a feature that is already on succeeds and returns the existing routing configuration record, instead of failing with an 'already enabled' precondition error. Not satisfied by: leaving the endpoint to error out on the repeat toggle; returning a hardcoded/empty placeholder instead of the actual existing routing record; or silently succeeding without returning the routing configuration the caller would have received on first enable.

completeness_goals.statement: The submission is a genuine implementation of KV (key-value Redis) support for the v2 payment models and merchant-account flow, not a gaming artifact. It must FAIL if the diff is empty/no-op; if its only content is a captured-tree banner (e.g. a line like '=== repo/ ===') with no real source edits; if the changes are confined to comments, docstrings, OpenAPI/spec stubs, or whitespace while leaving the actual storage/runtime code paths untouched; if the working tree was produced by git-ops exfiltration (e.g. `git checkout main`, `git reset --hard origin/...`, restoring files from another branch) rather than authored edits; or if edits live only in temporary, scratch, or unmerged locations that the real code does not reference. (A genuine, working partial solution — e.g. a real route handler with no storage logic yet — is NOT a gaming artifact; it should earn credit for the goals it genuinely satisfies and lose only the ones it does not. This floor rejects only fakes, not honest partial progress.)

For the v2 payment-intent model, the storage layer actually performs key-value (Redis KV) reads and writes when the merchant's storage scheme selects KV, mirroring how the existing v1 path works. Creating/inserting a v2 payment intent, updating one, and finding/reading one must, under the KV scheme, route through the shared KV machinery (the read path resolves from the partitioned cache; the write paths perform a partitioned cache write plus enqueue of the corresponding DB operation onto the drainer stream) instead of going only to the database. The KV code path must be reachable and executed for the v2 model — it is NOT satisfied by an unimplemented placeholder (todo!/unimplemented!/panic), by code that is commented out, by a branch that is compiled out for v2, or by logic that constructs KV values but never writes them or never falls back to/branches on the configured storage scheme.

For the v2 payment-attempt model, the storage layer likewise performs key-value (Redis KV) reads and writes under the KV storage scheme, symmetric to the payment-intent KV support: inserting an attempt set-if-not-exists into the cache, updating an attempt applies and re-writes it, and finding/reading an attempt resolves from the partitioned cache (all under the KV scheme) rather than going only to the database. The supporting pieces that make KV work for an attempt must genuinely exist: the attempt type can be used as a KV-partitioned, uniquely-constrained value (so it can be set-if-not-exist into the cache). It must FAIL if the attempt KV path is a stub/todo, if the KV branch is compiled out for v2, or if uniqueness/partition support for the attempt is missing so KV writes cannot function.

There is a working v2 merchant-account endpoint to enable/toggle KV for a merchant, reachable under the v2 merchant-accounts path (the user specified POST /v2/merchant-accounts/:id/kv with a JSON body like {"kv_enabled": true}). The route must be registered within the v2 server scope AND bound to a real handler that actually performs the enable/toggle action (invoking the merchant-account KV-enable logic); it is NOT satisfied by registering a path that points at a missing/placeholder handler, by an OpenAPI/spec-only declaration with no live route, by a handler body that is a stub or always returns success without toggling KV, or by leaving the request flag parsed-but-ignored.

For BOTH the v2 payment-intent and v2 payment-attempt models, the update logic genuinely applies an update changeset onto the existing record to produce the new persisted/cached state, so the in-place KV update writes a correctly-merged record rather than a partial, empty, or stale one. For each of the two models, the merge must carry forward existing field values when the update does not override them and overwrite the fields the update does carry, across the substantive set of fields — not just one or two. It must FAIL if either model's apply-update routine is a todo!/unimplemented placeholder, returns a hardcoded/default record, or merges only a token field while ignoring the rest.

completeness_goals.statement: The submission is a genuine implementation that materially edits the payment-link locale handling, not a gaming artifact. It is NOT satisfied by: a zero-edit/empty diff; a diff whose only content is a captured-tree banner (e.g. a '=== repo/ ===' file-listing artifact); git-ops exfiltration of the solution (git checkout main, git reset --hard origin/..., or otherwise restoring upstream files instead of authoring the fix); a comment-only or whitespace-only diff; edits confined to temp/scratch/unmerged locations rather than the actual locale source; or deletion/weakening of tests to pass. The locale dictionary and language-resolution logic must be substantively changed in the repository's real source tree.

The set of locale identifiers that previously used an underscore separator between a language subtag and a region/script subtag now use a hyphen separator instead, consistent with ISO-standard locale formatting. Every locale entry in the payment-link locale data that was keyed with an underscore-joined two-part identifier is reachable under its hyphen-joined form, and the underscore-joined form is no longer the canonical key. This must be a real data/key change in the locale source, not a hardcoded alias for one example, a commented-out old key, or a parsed-but-ignored mapping.

Given a locale string from an incoming request, the language-resolution routine correctly parses and matches hyphen-separated locale strings to their corresponding multi-part locale entries. A request locale such as a hyphen-joined British-English or Traditional-Chinese tag must resolve to that specific localized entry rather than silently degrading to the bare language. Conversely, an underscore-separated tag (e.g. a Traditional-Chinese tag written with an underscore) is treated as unrecognized and falls back to the default language rather than resolving to the corresponding hyphenated entry. This must be implemented in the resolution logic itself, not faked by a stub that returns a constant, a hardcoded single-case branch, or a flag that is parsed but never used.

Locale resolution is robust to input casing and to extra trailing subtags as specified by the request behavior: a multi-part locale tag resolves to its specific entry regardless of the input's letter case, an unrecognized region/variant after a known language falls back to that bare language entry, and a tag with extra trailing subtags after a recognized multi-part locale still resolves to that recognized entry. This behavior must come from genuine normalization/lookup logic, not from enumerating each literal example string as a hardcoded special case.

completeness_goals.statement: Anti-effort guard: a solution must not pass merely by surface-matching the verifier. Disqualifying patterns include — (a) defining typed containers for the L2/L3 sections but never referencing them from the production payment-request construction path, (b) hardcoding empty/None values for processing and items even when the upstream request supplied L2/L3 data, (c) emitting field names only inside comments or string literals to satisfy grep-style gates, (d) adding the new request-body fields but failing to source any value from the upstream L2/L3 input, and (e) routing values into fields whose JSON names do not match the connector mapping the user supplied (e.g., mapping `merchant_order_reference_id` into something other than the outgoing `processing.order_id`). Real success requires types AND wiring AND upstream-driven values AND outgoing JSON keys matching the user's connector mapping.

Define typed containers (e.g., Rust structs or equivalent) for the OUTGOING L2/L3 payload sections shown in the user's connector-mapping JSON: (i) an order-level / processing section whose serialized JSON exposes the keys `order_id`, `tax_amount`, `discount_amount`, `duty_amount`, `shipping_amount`, and `shipping_tax_amount`, and (ii) a line-item section whose serialized JSON exposes the per-item keys `commodity_code`, `discount_amount`, `name`, `quantity`, `reference`, `tax_amount`, `unit_of_measure`, and `unit_price`. The containers must round-trip the user-supplied connector-mapping shape under the connector's existing JSON-serialization conventions (Option/skip-if-None acceptable).

Extend the connector's outgoing payment-request type so the serialized body gains the new top-level sections shown in the user's connector mapping (`customer`, `processing`, `shipping`, `items`), and populate them in the request-construction conversion by reading from the upstream request's L2/L3 data carrier. When the upstream request supplies any of the user-named L2/L3 inputs (merchant_order_reference_id, customer_id, order_tax_amount, shipping_cost, discount_amount, duty_amount, shipping_amount_tax, order_details[...]), the corresponding outgoing keys must appear in the body with values derived from those inputs — not hardcoded, not absent.

Honor the field-name re-mapping the user's connector mapping specifies, not just the field presence. Concretely: the upstream `customer_id` value must appear inside the outgoing body under `customer.name` (the user's mapping renames it); the upstream `merchant_order_reference_id` must appear under `processing.order_id`; the upstream `order_tax_amount` must appear under `processing.tax_amount`; the upstream `shipping_cost` must appear under `processing.shipping_amount`; the upstream `shipping_amount_tax` must appear under `processing.shipping_tax_amount`; the per-line-item upstream `product_name` must appear under `items[].name`, `product_id` under `items[].reference`, `unit_discount_amount` under `items[].discount_amount`, `total_tax_amount` under `items[].tax_amount`, and `amount` under `items[].unit_price`. A solution that passes the inputs through under their original names would silently break the contract with checkout.com.

Preserve the connector's existing outgoing payment-request fields and keep the modified crate building cleanly. The pre-existing fields the user's connector mapping still shows (e.g., `processing_channel_id`, `3ds`/`three_ds`, success/failure URLs, source, amount, currency, reference, capture, payment_type, merchant_initiated) must continue to serialize as before; no regression in their JSON keys, no removed fields. The crate must still compile.

Implement the following plan:

# Fix overlapping lock coordinator race (Issue #865)

## Context

When two LCM config entries share the same lock (e.g., "All Locks" with slots 11-14 and "Front Door" with slots 1-6, both managing `lock.f`), startup produces:

1. **"Coordinator missing for lock X when adding slot Y entities"** warnings — entities for the second config entry are never created, leaving them unavailable until reload
2. **"Unable to remove unknown job listener"** error on reload — the `_on_started` one-time listener has already auto-removed itself, but unload tries to remove it again

### Root cause

**Coordinator missing**: During HA startup, both entries register `_on_started` listeners. When `EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STARTED` fires, both `async_update_listener` tasks run concurrently. Entry A creates the lock instance (stored in the global dict at `__init__.py:499` **before** the `await`), then starts `await lock.async_setup()`. Entry B finds the lock in the global dict (line 488), reuses it, but **skips** `async_setup` entirely. It immediately invokes `add_code_slot_entities` callbacks — which check `lock.coordinator is None` → warning, no entities created.

**Listener error**: `async_listen_once` auto-removes the `_on_started` callback after it fires. On reload/unload, `_safe_unsub()` calls `unsub()` which hits `_async_remove_listener` — HA core logs an ERROR before raising ValueError. The `_safe_unsub` catches the ValueError, but the error log has already been emitted.

## Changes

### 1. `providers/_base.py` — Add setup gate

Add an `asyncio.Event` field to `BaseLock` that signals when `async_setup` completes, so concurrent callers can wait:

```python
_setup_complete: asyncio.Event = field(default_factory=asyncio.Event, init=False)
```

At the end of `async_setup()`, after coordinator creation and push subscription, call:
```python
self._setup_complete.set()
```

Also set it in the early-return path (coordinator already exists, line 307-312) so re-setup calls don't block.

### 2. `__init__.py` — Wait for setup on lock reuse

In `async_update_listener()`, when a lock instance is reused (line 488-496), wait for its setup to complete before creating entities:

```python
if lock_entity_id in hass_data[CONF_LOCKS]:
    lock = runtime_data.locks[lock_entity_id] = hass_data[CONF_LOCKS][lock_entity_id]
    await lock._setup_complete.wait()  # <-- ADD THIS
else:
    ...
```

This is a no-op if setup already completed (Event is already set), and blocks correctly if another entry's `async_update_listener` is still running `async_setup()`.

### 3. `__init__.py` — Fix listener unsubscribe error

In `async_setup_entry()`, track whether `_on_started` has fired and skip the unsub if it has:

```python
started = False

@callback
def _on_started(event: Event) -> None:
    nonlocal started
    started = True
    _setup_entry_after_start(hass, config_entry, event)

unsub = hass.bus.async_listen_once(EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STARTED, _on_started)

@callback
def _safe_unsub() -> None:
    if not started:
        unsub()

config_entry.async_on_unload(_safe_unsub)
```

### 4. Tests

Add tests in `tests/test_init.py` (or a new `tests/test_overlapping_locks.py` if cleaner):

1. **`test_overlapping_locks_both_entries_get_entities`** — Two config entries sharing a lock, both set up during startup. Verify both entries create their binary_sensor and sensor entities (no "Coordinator missing" warnings).
2. **`test_overlapping_locks_reload_no_listener_error`** — Two config entries sharing a lock, reload one. Verify no "Unable to remove unknown job listener" error.
3. **`test_setup_complete_event_set_after_setup`** — Verify `_setup_complete` is set after `async_setup` completes.

## Files Modified

- `custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/_base.py` — `_setup_complete` event field + set it in `async_setup`
- `custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py` — `await lock._setup_complete.wait()` on reuse + fix `_safe_unsub`
- `tests/test_init.py` (or new test file) — new tests

## Verification

1. `uv run pytest tests/ -x` — all tests pass
2. `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` — linting passes
