completeness_goals.statement: ANTI-EFFORT FLOOR — do not introduce unrelated refactors, rename public symbols outside the in-scope modules, restructure unaffected files, modify CI/lint/pre-commit configuration, bump dependencies, or reformat untouched code. Changes must stay scoped to: (a) the overlapping-lock race fix (PR #900), (b) the one-time-listener unsubscribe fix (PR #900), (c) the encapsulation/refactor the user requested on top of (a)+(b), (d) the directly associated tests, and (e) the three substantive Copilot-review fixes the user explicitly accepted on PR #899 (in-progress clearing scoped to userCode updates, entry-title in duplicate notifications, correct slot in task name). Cleanups that are locally defensible but outside this scope are out of scope. EXPLICIT DEGENERATE / EXFILTRATION PATTERNS THAT VIOLATE THIS FLOOR (non-exhaustive but each pattern below is individually disqualifying): (a) ZERO-EDIT + LARGE CAPTURED-TREE PATCH — a final.patch in which the agent performed no real Edit/Write ops against the in-scope files but the captured diff is large because it snapshots the working tree, vendored deps, build artifacts, lockfile churn, generated files, or `__pycache__` / `.pyc` / `node_modules` content; (b) GIT-OPS EXFILTRATION — using git plumbing to import code from outside the buggy base state, including but not limited to `git checkout main`, `git checkout origin/main -- <path>`, `git reset --hard origin/<branch>`, `git reset --hard <sha>`, `git fetch <remote> <ref> && git checkout <ref>`, `git fetch ... && git reset --hard FETCH_HEAD`, `git cherry-pick <sha>`, `git revert <sha>` of the buggy-state synthesis commit, `git pull`, `git merge origin/<branch>`, or `git apply` of an externally-sourced patch — the agent must produce the fix by editing files in the working tree, not by importing the upstream fixed state; (c) COMMENT-ONLY OR WHITESPACE-ONLY DIFFS — a patch whose substantive content is exclusively added/removed comments, docstrings, blank-line reflow, trailing-whitespace strip, tab-vs-space reformatting, or import-reordering with no executable-code change addressing goals 1-11; (d) TEST DELETION OR SKIP — removing existing tests, marking them `@pytest.mark.skip` / `@pytest.mark.xfail` / `pytest.skip(...)` / `unittest.skip` / `if False:`, commenting out test bodies, deleting test files, neutering assertions to `assert True` / `pass`, or otherwise disabling tests in lieu of fixing the production code those tests exercise. SCORING: this goal carries weight 0.00 — it is a true floor, not a weighted axis. A judge that finds this goal violated should CAP the task's total rubric score at 0.70 (i.e. cannot reach the full 1.00 even if every other goal scores 1.00). A judge that finds this goal satisfied does not add anything to the score.

Add a setup-completion signaling primitive on the lock base class so that code which races with first-time setup can block until that setup has finished. The user explicitly named `asyncio.Event` as their proposed mechanism in the Turn 0 plan ('Add an asyncio.Event field to BaseLock that signals when async_setup completes'); an `asyncio.Event` satisfies this goal directly. Any other awaitable completion primitive (asyncio.Future, Condition variable, etc.) is also acceptable PROVIDED it preserves the same observable semantics: callers awaiting the primitive block until setup is signaled, and the primitive can be set multiple times without raising. The primitive must release waiters on every exit path from the first-time-setup routine: normal completion, the early-return path taken when the coordinator already exists, AND the exception/failure path (e.g., via try/finally or equivalent control flow). A stub that creates the primitive but never signals it, or only signals on the happy path, does not satisfy this goal.

When a second config entry reuses a lock instance that already exists in the shared lock registry, the code path that creates entities for that second entry must first await the setup-completion primitive from goal_1 before touching the coordinator or registering entities. The await must go through a public/encapsulated method on the lock class (e.g., something like `await lock.async_wait_for_setup()` — any sensible public method name is acceptable). Reaching into a private attribute (e.g., `await lock._setup_complete.wait()`) from outside the lock module does NOT satisfy this goal, because the user explicitly objected to that style.

Fix the 'Unable to remove unknown job listener' error on reload/unload by changing the unsubscribe logic so it never tries to remove a one-time HOMEASSISTANT_STARTED listener that has already fired (and therefore already removed itself). The user proposed the canonical mechanism in the Turn 0 plan: a captured `started` boolean flag, set by the `_on_started` callback itself via the Python `nonlocal` keyword, then checked by `_safe_unsub` (`if not started: unsub()`). Implementations that use this exact pattern (a captured-flag closure with `nonlocal`) satisfy this goal. Alternative state-based avoidance patterns are also acceptable PROVIDED they preserve the same observable property: `_safe_unsub` short-circuits when the listener has already auto-removed itself, so HA core's `_async_remove_listener` is never called for the missing entry — acceptable alternatives include checking a Home Assistant core-state predicate that proves the started event has already passed (e.g., `hass.state != CoreState.starting`, with attention to the `CoreState.stopping` / pre-`CoreState.running` edge cases the user raised in Turns 85 and 88). Using try/except ValueError to swallow the error after-the-fact does NOT satisfy this goal, because HA core still logs the error before the exception is caught.

Encapsulate the first-time setup body so the base lock class exposes a single public setup entry point that always signals the completion primitive (per goal_1) and delegates the actual work to a protected/overridable hook that subclass providers extend. After this refactor, subclass providers (the existing providers, plus any future ones) must be able to add provider-specific setup logic by overriding the protected hook — not by overriding the public entry point and re-implementing the completion signaling themselves.

Add at least one test that demonstrates the overlapping-lock race is fixed. The user explicitly named the test `test_overlapping_locks_both_entries_get_entities` in the Turn 0 plan; that name is preferred but not required, as long as the test does what that name describes: set up two config entries that share the same underlying lock, then assert (a) no 'Coordinator missing' (or equivalent) warning is logged for the second entry, AND (b) the second entry's entities are actually created / its coordinator is populated. Assertions must be on observable behavior (entities exist, coordinator is not None, log text), not on the private completion primitive itself.

Add a regression test that genuinely exercises the listener-unsubscribe code path from goal_3. The user named `test_overlapping_locks_reload_no_listener_error` as the second new test in the Turn 0 plan; that name is preferred but not required, as long as the test: drives the code path where the one-time HOMEASSISTANT_STARTED listener is actually registered (i.e., set up while HA core is still starting, not already running), lets the started event fire so the listener auto-removes itself, then triggers unload/reload, and finally asserts that no 'Unable to remove unknown job' error string is present in the captured log output. A test that runs entirely while HA core is already in the running state — and therefore never registers the one-time listener — does NOT satisfy this goal because it is a no-op assertion that would pass even with the bug present.

Add tests covering the early-return branches of the duplicate-code handler — at minimum, the cases (a) the slot identifier is cleared/None before the deferred task runs, (b) no config entry manages the slot identifier in question, and (c) the lookup for the enabled-toggle entity returns nothing. Each branch must be exercised by a distinct test (or distinct parametrize case) that observably shows the handler returned early without producing a side effect that the non-early-return path would produce.

Fix the PR #899 in-progress-slot clearing race so that the in-progress tracking field (e.g. `_set_in_progress_code_slot`) is only cleared on Z-Wave JS Value Updates that actually carry a new user-code payload (the `LOCK_USERCODE_PROPERTY` value, or the equivalent property name in the codebase). Updates carrying only user-id-status information (`userIdStatus`, or the equivalent) must NOT clear the in-progress slot, because Copilot review comment #4 (acknowledged by the user in Turn 20) demonstrated that the `userIdStatus` Value Update can arrive before the duplicate-code notification handler runs, racing the clear against the duplicate detection. The behavioral requirement is: a value update whose property indicates a status-only change must leave the in-progress slot intact; a value update whose property indicates an actual user-code change MAY clear it.

Include the affected LCM config entry's title in the user-visible duplicate-code notification / error message produced when a slot's code is rejected as a duplicate (Copilot review comment #5 on PR #899, acknowledged by user in Turn 20). The current message shows only the lock entity_id and the slot number; the fix must add identifying information for the LCM config entry that owns the slot (typically the entry's `title`) so users with multiple LCM entries can identify which entry to fix. The format is not pinned — any phrasing that makes the entry identifiable to the user (e.g. parenthetical `(config entry <title>)`, prefix, suffix) satisfies the goal. NOT satisfied by: adding the entry title only to a code comment, a docstring, or a `logger.info` / `logger.debug` line without changing the user-facing notification body text. NOT satisfied by: changing only the test fixture's expected message string without altering the production code that produces the notification. NOT satisfied by: appending the config entry's id (a UUID-like opaque slug) instead of the human-readable title — the user-facing surface needs an identifier a human can map to a UI entry, not an internal id.

Fix the task / log / metric name slot when the duplicate-code-handler falls back to using the previously-tracked in-progress slot (`_set_in_progress_code_slot`) because the incoming `code_slot` is 0 / sentinel (Copilot review comment #6 on PR #899, acknowledged by user in Turn 20). The current code uses the incoming slot value (0) when naming the deferred task / log / notification id; the fix must substitute the tracked in-progress slot value in those name strings when the incoming value is 0, so observers see a meaningful slot number rather than the placeholder. NOT satisfied by: changing the name string template (or the surrounding scaffolding) but still interpolating the incoming `code_slot` value, so observers still see `0` at runtime. NOT satisfied by: adding the substitution only inside a debug-only branch, a conditional that never executes on the duplicate-code fallback path, or a comment describing what the value should be. NOT satisfied by: renaming the variable to a more descriptive name without actually swapping the substituted value when code_slot == 0.

Review the repository's TODO.md and remove or revise entries that are no longer needed or relevant — explicitly: items that have already been completed by the work delivered in this session (PR #900 race fix + PR #899 duplicate-notification fixes) or items whose factual content is stale (e.g., year/version references that have aged out, sub-bullets describing work that has since landed). The output must be a non-trivial edit to TODO.md (at least one obsolete line removed or visibly revised, not a whitespace/typo-only diff). NOT satisfied by: leaving TODO.md untouched, deleting the entire file, or making a no-op formatting-only change that does not actually drop or revise any stale entry.

completeness_goals.statement: The submission must show non-trivial, load-bearing changes to the two source files that govern batched generation with prompt caches (the cache-types module and the generate module). Both files must remain importable (no SyntaxError, no removal of pre-existing public cache classes). A patch that is empty, comment-only, or that satisfies tests purely by deleting the buggy-state error-raising path without supplying a working replacement scores zero on this gate AND caps the overall rubric score at 0.0 regardless of what any other goal would otherwise award. This is a hard floor: if the judge concludes the patch is a stub-deletion / no-op / hardcoded-return masquerade, the rubric reward for the trial is 0.0 even if structural greps on goals 2 or 6 happen to fire.

Per-sequence states for the cache type used by Mamba-style layers (the layer type that previously could not participate in batched generation with prompt caches) can be composed into a multi-sequence batched state and decomposed back to single sequences. Specifically: combining N single-sequence states must produce a state whose underlying buffers have batch dimension N along axis 0 with per-sequence values preserved; given that batched state, recovering any single sequence must return a single-sequence state whose buffers slice cleanly back to the originating values. Mechanism-agnostic — classmethod, instancemethod, free helper, or inline composition inside the generation-time dispatch all satisfy the goal as long as the round-trip is correct on both shape (batch dim) and values. NOT satisfied by: a stub that returns hardcoded shapes, a no-op that copies one input to all positions, a function that raises NotImplementedError, or any implementation that does not actually concatenate the per-sequence buffer payloads along axis 0.

The internal helper in the generate module that combines a list of per-sequence cache stacks into a batched cache stack must no longer raise the buggy-state ValueError ('does not yet support batching with history') for the Mamba-style cache type or for the container type that holds a mixed-cache stack (the per-layer composite used by hybrid models). Given N input stacks composed of these previously-unsupported types, it must return a single batched stack of the same length, with each layer's batched representation correctly carrying batch-dim N. Dispatch mechanism unconstrained — explicit isinstance branches, polymorphic method dispatch on the cache object, type-registered handlers, or a uniform recursive walk all satisfy the goal. NOT satisfied by: deleting the raise-ValueError line and returning the first input unchanged, returning an empty list, returning a list of None placeholders, raising a different exception with the same effect, or any change whose only effect on the error is renaming it. The replacement must actually combine the N inputs into a true batched stack — verified end-to-end by goals 1 and 3.

Heterogeneous per-layer composite caches (the layer container type that mixes a Mamba-style state slot and an attention-style state slot, as used by the model the user named) support the same batched composition / per-sequence decomposition as the simple cache type in goal_1, with sub-cache ordering preserved (the Mamba-style slot stays Mamba-style on the way in and out, the attention-style slot stays attention-style on the way in and out). Round-trip on the composite: N single-sequence composites → one batched composite of width N → recover any of the N → original single-sequence composite for that index (shape and values match). API surface unconstrained — methods on the composite, recursion inside the merge helper from goal_2, or a free routine all satisfy this provided the round-trip preserves both order and per-slot semantics. NOT satisfied by: collapsing both sub-slots to a single sub-type, replacing the attention slot with a Mamba-style slot (or vice-versa) to make the dispatch easier, or any implementation where the recovered single-sequence composite has a different sub-cache class layout than the input.

When a batched prefill uses right-side padding so that different sequences contribute different numbers of real prompt tokens, the cache stores enough per-sequence information for the attention-mask routine to mark positions beyond each sequence's real length as invalid. Concretely: a 2-sequence batched cache prepared with right-padding pattern [2, 0] over a sequence-length-5 cache must subsequently produce, via whatever mask-construction routine the cache exposes, a mask where sequence 0 has exactly 3 'valid' positions at the front and sequence 1 has all 5 positions 'valid'. The 'valid' polarity (True or False) may match either convention provided the all-valid row is uniform. Mechanism-agnostic — an attribute named anything (or no named attribute, just a thread of arguments) is fine; only the end-to-end mask must be correct. Implement the following plan:

# Plan: Implement `microtokenizer.py`

## Context

First script in the no-magic repository. Phase 1 of the implementation sequence — establishes the project's first working educational script. BPE tokenization was chosen as the entry point because it requires no autograd, has clear success criteria, and is the first step in the learning path ("How text becomes numbers").

**Target file:** `01-foundations/microtokenizer.py`
**Expected:** ~180-200 lines, < 2 min runtime, zero dependencies

---

## Implementation Structure

### Section 0: File Thesis + Reference

```python
"""
How text becomes numbers -- the compression algorithm hiding inside every LLM.
Byte-Pair Encoding learns a vocabulary by iteratively merging the most frequent
adjacent token pairs, then encodes new text by replaying those merges in priority order.
"""
# Reference: Philip Gage, "A New Algorithm for Data Compression" (1994).
# GPT-2's byte-level BPE variant (Radford et al., 2019) starts from raw bytes
# rather than characters -- that's the version implemented here.
```

### Section 1: Imports + Seed

- `os`, `urllib.request`, `collections.Counter`
- `random.seed(42)` (repo convention, BPE itself is deterministic)

### Section 2: Constants

| Constant | Value | Rationale |
|----------|-------|-----------|
| `NUM_MERGES` | 256 | Vocab = 512 tokens. Enough compression for demo, fast training. |
| `DATA_URL` | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karpathy/makemore/master/names.txt` | |
| `DATA_FILE` | `"names.txt"` | Cached locally, gitignored |

Signpost: production tokenizers use 50K+ merges on gigabytes.

### Section 3: Data Loading

**`load_data(url, filename) -> bytes`** — Download-and-cache pattern via urllib.

Convert corpus to `list[int]` (byte values 0-255). Print stats: byte count, base vocab size, planned merges.

Key intuition comment: bytes-as-base-vocab eliminates "unknown tokens" — every input is representable.

### Section 4: BPE Training

Three functions:

1. **`get_pair_counts(token_ids) -> Counter`**
   - Count adjacent pairs via `zip(ids, ids[1:])`
   - O(n) per call

2. **`apply_merge(token_ids, pair, new_id) -> list[int]`**
   - Left-to-right scan, greedy replacement
   - Why comment: overlapping pairs resolve left-to-right (standard BPE convention)
   - Signpost: O(n) per merge; production uses priority queues for O(n log n) total

3. **`train_bpe(token_ids, num_merges) -> list[tuple[tuple[int, int], int]]`**
   - Main loop: count pairs → find max → merge → record rule
   - Returns ordered merge table (index = priority, `new_id = 256 + index`)
   - Early break if no pairs remain
   - Print progress every 32 steps: merge index, pair, frequency, sequence length

Key intuition: each merge absorbs the most redundancy per step — greedy compression that naturally discovers morphological units ("play" + "ing") without linguistic rules.

### Section 5: Encoding + Decoding

4. **`build_vocab(merges) -> dict[int, bytes]`**
   - Base: `{i: bytes([i]) for i in range(256)}`
   - Merged: `vocab[new_id] = vocab[a] + vocab[b]`
   - Recursive expansion makes decoding trivial — every token maps to definite bytes

5. **`encode(text, merges) -> list[int]`**
   - Convert text to bytes → apply merges in **priority order** (NOT frequency order on new text)
   - Critical "why" comment: priority order ensures deterministic tokenization; re-counting would make output input-dependent
   - Signpost: O(n * M) naive encoding; production uses trie structures for O(n)

6. **`decode(token_ids, vocab) -> str`**
   - Lookup + concatenate + UTF-8 decode
   - Intuition: decode is just a lookup table — round-trip correctness is guaranteed by construction

### Section 6: Inference Demo

Print output in four blocks:

1. **Round-trip tests**: 6 test strings (common name, uncommon name, hyphenated, apostrophe, empty, single char) — each shows `[PASS/FAIL]` with encoded tokens and decoded result.

2. **Compression ratio**: Full corpus byte count vs BPE token count. Must be >= 1.5x.

3. **Top 20 merges**: Show each merge's component tokens and resulting token in human-readable form.

4. **Tokenization example**: One name broken into bytes → tokens → pieces.

---

## Functions Summary

| Function | Signature | Purpose |
|----------|-----------|---------|
| `load_data` | `(url: str, filename: str) -> bytes` | Download and cache dataset |
| `get_pair_counts` | `(token_ids: list[int]) -> Counter` | Count adjacent pair frequencies |
| `apply_merge` | `(token_ids: list[int], pair: tuple[int, int], new_id: int) -> list[int]` | Replace pair occurrences with new token |
| `train_bpe` | `(token_ids: list[int], num_merges: int) -> list[...]` | Learn merge rules from corpus |
| `build_vocab` | `(merges: list[...]) -> dict[int, bytes]` | Build token-to-bytes lookup |
| `encode` | `(text: str, merges: list[...]) -> list[int]` | Tokenize string to IDs |
| `decode` | `(token_ids: list[int], vocab: dict[int, bytes]) -> str` | Detokenize IDs to string |

---

## Comment Plan

| Type | Count | Key Locations |
|------|-------|---------------|
| File thesis | 1 | Top docstring |
| Section headers | 5 | Constants, Data Loading, BPE Training, Encoding/Decoding, Inference |
| "Why" comments | 4+ | Left-to-right merge, priority order encoding, bytes-as-base, greedy compression |
| Math-to-code | 2 | Pair counting formulation, compression ratio |
| Intuition | 3+ | No unknown tokens, morphology emergence, decode simplicity |
| Signpost | 3 | 256 vs 50K merges, O(n*M) vs trie, naive vs priority queue |

Target density: 30-40% comment/blank lines.

---

## Verification

1. `python 01-foundations/microtokenizer.py` exits 0, prints training + inference
2. All round-trip tests print `[PASS]`
3. Compression ratio >= 1.5x
4. Runtime < 2 minutes (expected: 10-30 seconds)
5. No imports outside stdlib
6. Line count ~180-200

If this plan can be broken down into multiple independent tasks, consider using the TeamCreate tool to create a team and parallelize the work.

Audit changelog entries for all commits since the last release.

## Process

1. **Find the last release tag:**
   ```bash
   git tag --sort=-version:refname | head -1
   ```

2. **List all commits since that tag:**
   ```bash
   git log <tag>..HEAD --oneline
   ```

3. **Read each package's [Unreleased] section:**
   - packages/ai/CHANGELOG.md
   - packages/tui/CHANGELOG.md
   - packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md

4. **For each commit, check:**
   - Skip: changelog updates, doc-only changes, release housekeeping
   - Determine which package(s) the commit affects (use `git show <hash> --stat`)
   - Verify a changelog entry exists in the affected package(s)
   - For external contributions (PRs), verify format: `Description ([#N](url) by [@user](url))`

5. **Cross-package duplication rule:**
   Changes in `ai`, `agent` or `tui` that affect end users should be duplicated to `coding-agent` changelog, since coding-agent is the user-facing package that depends on them.

6. **Report:**
   - List commits with missing entries
   - List entries that need cross-package duplication
   - Add any missing entries directly

## Changelog Format Reference

Sections (in order):
- `### Breaking Changes` - API changes requiring migration
- `### Added` - New features
- `### Changed` - Changes to existing functionality
- `### Fixed` - Bug fixes
- `### Removed` - Removed features

Attribution:
- Internal: `Fixed foo ([#123](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/123))`
- External: `Added bar ([#456](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/456) by [@user](https://github.com/user))`

completeness_goals.statement: The submission must be a genuine implementation of the requested backward-compatibility behavior, not a gaming artifact. Reject (flag) if the diff is empty or a no-op; if it consists only of a captured repository-tree banner (e.g. a diff whose entire content is a '=== repo/ ===' style listing) with no real code change; if it only contains git-operation exfiltration such as 'git checkout main', 'git reset --hard origin/...', or restoring tracked files instead of editing them; if the only changes are comments, docstrings, or whitespace with no behavioral effect; or if changes live solely in temporary, throwaway, or unmerged locations (e.g. /tmp, a scratch file, a test-only helper) that the production caching code path never invokes. The legacy-fallback logic must be reachable from the strategy methods that production training actually calls when checking or loading cached latents.

When the resolution-suffixed cached-latent entry is absent, the existence/validity check and the load path must fall back to the legacy entry that has no resolution suffix and accept it when its stored array dimensions match what the requested bucket resolution expects. The loaded latents and their associated metadata (such as original size and crop values) must come from that legacy entry and be returned with correct values. This fallback must be exercised by the actual caching-strategy methods that production code calls, not by a stub that always returns a fixed answer, a hardcoded shape, or commented-out code.

The size/shape validation of the legacy unsuffixed entry must read only the array's stored metadata header to obtain its dimensions, without decompressing or reading the full array body. Concretely, the number of bytes consumed from the latent array member during the existence check must be header-sized (orders of magnitude smaller than the full array), and a legacy file whose member carries a valid array header but a truncated/missing body must still yield a non-crashing, correct accept/reject decision. A solution that loads the whole array (e.g. fully materializing it) to read its shape does not satisfy this, even if it returns the right boolean. This must not be satisfied by a stub or hardcoded return that skips reading the file, nor by a commented-out or unreachable header-reading code path.

The new legacy-fallback behavior must be scoped so that it applies to the SD1/SDXL caching path and does NOT alter the behavior of other (non-SD) model strategies. If the fallback is implemented in a shared base class, it must be gated (e.g. opted into only by the SD1/SDXL path) so that strategies which did not previously perform this fallback continue to behave exactly as before. Other model strategies must not start silently accepting or loading legacy unsuffixed caches as a side effect of this change. This scoping must be functionally enforced by the code path actually taken at runtime, not satisfied by a comment, a parsed-but-ignored flag, or a stub.

The validity check and load path must remain correct at the boundaries: (a) a legacy unsuffixed entry whose stored dimensions do NOT match the requested bucket resolution must be rejected, not silently loaded as if valid — acceptance must be conditioned on the metadata-derived shape actually matching the expectation; and (b) when BOTH a suffixed entry and a legacy unsuffixed entry are present, the suffixed entry must win (its values and metadata are loaded) and the legacy fallback is consulted only when the suffixed entry is absent, preserving the pre-existing suffixed-path behavior. This must not be satisfied by a hardcoded rejection, a blanket accept, or a parsed-but-ignored shape; the decision must follow from the actual entry contents.
